subQuestions.questionText:
The information relates to Comfort Traders for the VAT period ended 31 January 2025. The VAT rate is 15%. The business is owned by Karen Botha. The sales of the business average R150 000 per month.

Calculate the VAT amounts in the table provided in the ANSWER BOOK. Indicate the effect of EACH item on the amount payable to SARS. Show an increase with a '+' and a decrease with a '–'. An example has been completed.

INFORMATION:
A. Amount owed to SARS on 1 January 2025: R51 500.
B. Transactions for January 2025:
- Example: Drawings of stock — Excl VAT R6 000, Incl VAT R6 900, VAT Amount R900
(i) Merchandise purchased — Incl VAT R221 720
(ii) Credit notes issued to customers — Excl VAT R12 000
(iii) Total sales — Incl VAT R187 795 (Certain goods, with a total selling price of R21 275 (including VAT), should have been recorded as zero-rated items.)
(iv) Bad debts written off — VAT amount R765
subQuestions.memoText:
VAT calculation table:

Opening balance: 51 500
Example (Drawings): 900 (given)

(i) Merchandise purchased: 221 720 x 15/115 OR 221 720 - 192 800 = -28 920 (decrease, reduces VAT payable)

(ii) Credit notes issued to customers: 12 000 x 15/100 OR 12 000 - 10 200 = -1 800 (decrease)

(iii) Total sales: (187 795 - 21 275) x 15/115 = 166 520 x 15/115 = +21 720 (increase)
   OR (163 300 - 18 500) x 15/100 = 144 800 x 15/100
   OR 24 495 - 2 775 = 21 720
   Note: if final answer shown with incorrect sign, award working marks only, not final mark

(iv) Bad debts written off: -765 (decrease, given)

VAT PAYABLE = 51 500 + 900 - 28 920 - 1 800 + 21 720 - 765 = 41 735
Accept 42 635 (one part correct)

Accept brackets for negative amounts. Total must include the opening balance.
Mark allocation: 10 marks total across the calculations.

subQuestions.questionText: Karen wants to deregister her business as a VAT vendor as she is unable to meet VAT deadlines for submissions. What advice would you give to Karen? State ONE point.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE valid point (2 marks). Part-marks for partial/unclear answer:
• If the business's turnover exceeds R1m p.a., it is compulsory to be registered and submit VAT returns.
• If submission deadline is not met, the business will have to pay penalties to SARS.
• She will not be able to claim back the VAT paid to suppliers.
• Karen should have a tax consultant who can remind her of tax period to file on time.
• Set up automated reminders through eFiling system.

subQuestions.questionText:
Epson Traders received a statement of account from a creditor, Canon Suppliers. The balance on the statement did not agree with that on the account of Canon Suppliers in the Creditors' Ledger of Epson Traders.

Use the table provided to indicate changes to the:
• Creditors' Ledger Account in the books of Epson Traders
• Statement of account received from Canon Suppliers

Write the amount and indicate increase (+) or decrease (-) with each amount.

INFORMATION:
A. Creditors' Ledger of Epson Traders – Canon Suppliers (CL9): Opening balance R69 800; 6 March Invoice 519 R26 300 (balance R96 100); 8 March Debit Note 104 R1 600 (balance R94 500); 14 March EFT 310 R45 500 (balance R49 000), Discount R7 000 (balance R42 000); 15 March Invoice 202 R13 800 (balance R55 800); 24 March Invoice 567 R20 000 (balance R75 800); 25 March Invoice 594 R17 100 (balance R92 900); 31 March Invoice 610 R9 000 (balance R101 900).

B. Statement of account from Canon Suppliers (dated 25 March 2025): Opening balance R69 800; 4 March Interest R400 (balance R70 200); 6 March Invoice 519 R23 600 (balance R93 800); 8 March Credit Note 164 R1 600 (balance R95 400); 14 March Receipt 7710 R45 500 (balance R49 900); 24 March Invoice 567 R20 000 (balance R69 900); 25 March Invoice 594 R19 000 (balance R88 900).

C. Differences noted:
(i) Canon Suppliers correctly levied interest of R400.
(ii) Invoice 519 was correct according to Canon Suppliers' statement.
(iii) Canon Suppliers made an error in recording the return of goods on 8 March 2025.
(iv) Epson Traders qualified for an early settlement discount on 14 March. Canon Suppliers granted only R5 000 as discount and promised to show this next month.
(v) Invoice 202 for R13 800 was recorded incorrectly in Epson's Creditors' Ledger - the invoice was from another creditor, Baron Suppliers.
(vi) A trade discount of 10% was deducted on invoice 594. Canon Suppliers will correct this next month.
(vii) Invoice 610 did not appear on the statement (after statement date).
subQuestions.memoText:
CREDITORS' RECONCILIATION TABLE:

Creditors Ledger Account of Epson Traders | Statement of Account from Canon Suppliers
Opening balances: 101 900 | 88 900

(i) Interest R400: Statement side: +400
(ii) Invoice 519 difference (26 300 - 23 600): Ledger: -2 700
(iii) Debit/Credit Note correction (-1 600 - 1 600): Statement: -3 200
(iv) Discount qualified for (7 000 - 5 000): Ledger: +2 000; Statement: -5 000
(v) Invoice 202 (Baron Suppliers, recorded incorrectly): Ledger: -13 800
(vi) Trade discount on Invoice 594 (19 000 - 17 100 = 1 900): Statement: -1 900
(vii) Invoice 610 (after statement date): Statement: +9 000

Final balances: 87 800 | 87 800

Mark allocation: 14 marks. Balances may be different but must include opening balances.
-1 for foreign items per line provided a mark is scored on that line (max could be -6).

subQuestions.questionText:
It was discovered that the purchasing manager, Senzo, had signed a fictitious invoice received from Prime Suppliers. The banking details of his son appeared on this invoice. The relevant payment was processed by the financial department.

Other than dismissing Senzo, provide:

subQuestions.questionText:
WOLLIES' WINTER GLOVES — The business manufactures winter gloves. The financial year ended on 28 February 2025. Owner: Jerry Classon. The business does not carry any work-in-progress stock and all items produced are sold.

Calculate the direct material cost for the year ended 28 February 2025.

Information A — Direct material cost:
- Opening stock: 6 000 metres at R55/metre = R330 000
- Purchases: 24 000 metres at R60/metre = R1 440 000
- Total available for use: 30 000 metres = R1 770 000
- Closing stock: 4 000 metres
- Direct materials issued for production: 26 000 metres
- Material is transferred to the factory using the weighted-average method.
- Due to good internal controls there were no missing or stolen material.
subQuestions.memoText:
Calculation using weighted-average method:
Weighted average cost per metre = $\frac{1\,770\,000}{30\,000} = R59$ per metre

Direct material cost = 26 000 x R59 = R1 534 000

Alternative workings:
• 1 770 000 - (4 000 x 59) = 1 770 000 - 236 000 = R1 534 000
• 1 770 000 x (26 000/30 000) = R1 534 000

Mark allocation: 4 marks (one part correct).

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the correct factory overhead cost for the year ended 28 February 2025.

Information B — Factory overhead cost: The bookkeeper calculated the factory overheads as R966 360. However, errors must be corrected:
(i) The entire telephone expense of R36 000 was used instead of 25% being allocated to the factory.
(ii) The closing stock of factory indirect material was understated by R2 800.
(iii) The bookkeeper correctly allocated the cleaner's wages to factory overheads. However, he neglected the increase of 6% p.a. effective from 1 January 2025. The cleaner earns R48 000 p.a. and spends half his time in the factory.
(iv) Water and electricity of R25 600 was allocated to the factory using the ratio 4:3:2 (factory:sales:office). This should have been 5:3:2.
subQuestions.memoText:
Calculation of correct factory overhead cost:

Incorrect total: 966 360

(i) Telephone correction: -27 000 (75% of R36 000 should NOT be in factory)
(ii) Indirect materials understated: -2 800
(iii) Cleaner's wages adjustment: (R48 000/2) x (6/100) x (2/12) = R240
   OR (4 000 x 6/100) OR (48 000/100)/2 = +240
(iv) Water and electricity correction: 
   Original (factory share 4/9 of R25 600 if R25 600 is total) - corrected calculation
   28 800 - 25 600 = 3 200 OR 32 000 - 28 800 = 3 200 OR 25 600 x 5/40 = 3 200
   = +3 200

Corrected factory overhead cost = 966 360 - 27 000 - 2 800 + 240 + 3 200 = R940 000

Mark allocation: 9 marks (one part correct). Final amount must include the opening total.

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the gross profit earned for the year ended 28 February 2025.

Given: Sales = R4 600 000; Direct labour cost = R876 000.
subQuestions.memoText:
Gross Profit calculation:

Gross Profit = Sales - (Direct material + Direct labour + Factory overheads)
= 4 600 000 - 1 534 000 (from 2.2.1) - 876 000 - 940 000 (from 2.2.2)
= 4 600 000 - 3 350 000
= R1 250 000

Mark allocation: 5 marks (one part correct).
Be alert to alternative workings such as ledger account or use of brackets.

subQuestions.questionText:
Jerry was satisfied with the performance during the current year and plans to increase production by 30% in the next financial year. He is confident that the demand will increase due to changing weather patterns.

• Comment on the level of production and the break-even points comparing the results for the current financial year with his plan for the next financial year. Provide TWO points, with figures.
• Calculate the increase in profits Jerry expects to earn from the year ended 28 February 2025 to the next financial year.

Information D — Other information:
- Units produced and sold: 28 Feb 2025: 40 000 pairs; Plan: 52 000 pairs
- Break-even point: 28 Feb 2025: 38 000 pairs; Plan: 38 400 pairs
- Selling price per pair: R115 both years
- Sales: R4 600 000 / R5 980 000
subQuestions.memoText:
PART 1 — Comment on production vs BEP (4 marks - TWO points with figures):

Expected responses for 4 marks:
• He made profit on 2 000 units (40 000 - 38 000) for the current year and expects more profit on 13 600 units (52 000 - 38 400) next year.
• He produced 2 000 units above the BEP (current year) and expects to produce 13 600 units above the BEP (next year).
• Anticipating increased profit on 11 600 units, as BEP expected to increase by 400 units (1.1%), while production projected to increase by 12 000 units (30%).

Expected response for 2 marks (max two marks in total - mark one optional response only):
• Production will increase from 40 000 units to 52 000 units / by 12 000 units.
• BEP will increase from 38 000 units to 38 400 units / by 400 units.

PART 2 — Calculate increase in profits (5 marks):

Contribution per unit:
• Current year: R115 - R75 = R40 per unit
• Next year: R115 - R67.50 = R47.50 per unit

Increase in profits = (13 600 x R47.50) - (2 000 x R40)
= R646 000 - R80 000
= R566 000

Mark allocation: 5 marks (one part correct).
subQuestions.topic: Cost Accounting — Break-even and Profit Analysis

subQuestions.questionText:
Give TWO possible reasons for the proposed increase in direct labour cost in the next financial year. Quote figures.

Given: Direct labour cost: 28 Feb 2025: R876 000 (R21.90/pair); Plan: R1 300 000 (R25.00/pair).
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO valid points (4 marks) — figures and trend required:

• DLC will increase (from R876 000) to R1 300 000 / by R424 000 / by 48%. Provision made for overtime / Production incentive bonuses set to be implemented which may be necessary to meet targets.

• Unit costs will increase (from R21.90) to R25.00 / by R3.10 / by 14%. He has accommodated annual inflationary increases or salary increase or introduced improved fringe benefits.

subQuestions.questionText:
Jerry has projected an increase of R304 000 for the total fixed costs.

• Provide TWO possible expense items he may have considered when making his projections. Give a different reason for each item identified.
• Explain why Jerry should not be concerned about this proposed increase in the total fixed costs. Provide ONE point with figures.
subQuestions.memoText:
PART 1 — TWO expense items with reasons (4 marks):

Accept any TWO of the following pairs:
• Depreciation on factory machinery — Additional machinery may be required for increased production.
• Indirect labour — The workload of the foreman/supervisor will increase / increase in minimum wage of cleaners.
• Water and electricity — Increased usage due to overtime hours.
• Indirect materials/consumable stores — More units must be cleaned or maintained / Increased office cleaning or packaging materials.
• Rent expenses — More rental space to accommodate the increase in production.
• Insurance — An increase in assets will require additional coverage.
• Repairs and maintenance — Increased production will lead to regular repairs and maintenance.
• Security — Need for more security personnel / advanced security system.
• Administration cost — Need to hire more office staff / Increased office work.

PART 2 — Why Jerry should not be concerned (2 marks):

Any ONE valid point with figures:
• The fixed cost per unit decreased (from R38.00) to R35.10 / by R2.90 / by 7.6% while the units produced increased.
OR
• Fixed cost per unit decreased (from R38.00) to R35.10 / by R2.90 / by 7.6% and he took advantage of economies of scale.

subQuestions.questionText:
HELEN'S ELECTRONICS — Helen Woods owns an electronics shop. Financial year ended 28 February 2025.

HEADPHONES (FIFO method applies)

Calculate the value of the closing stock on 28 February 2025, using the FIFO method.

INFORMATION:
A. Stock balances: 1 March 2024: 170 units at R145 = R24 650; 28 February 2025: 350 units.
B. Purchases: April 2024: 250 units at R165 = R41 250; June 2024: 300 units at R180 = R54 000; September 2024: 380 units at R135 = R51 300; December 2024: 320 units at R140 = R44 800. Total: 1 250 units = R191 350.
C. Carriage on purchases: R20 per unit (non-refundable, not included in B).
D. Returns: 80 headphones purchased in December 2024 returned to suppliers, R11 200.
E. Sales: 1 Mar - 31 Aug 2024: 680 units at R220 = R149 600; 1 Sep 2024 - 28 Feb 2025: 310 units at R220 = R68 200. Total: 990 units = R217 800.
subQuestions.memoText:
Closing stock on 28 February 2025 using FIFO:

Closing stock = 350 units
Net December purchases = 320 - 80 (returned) = 240 units
From September: 350 - 240 = 110 units

Unit cost (including carriage):
• December batch: R140 + R20 = R160 per unit
• September batch: R135 + R20 = R155 per unit

Closing stock = (240 x R160) + (110 x R155)
= R38 400 + R17 050
= R55 450

Alternative: (33 600 + 4 800) + (14 850 + 2 200) = 55 450

Mark allocation: 5 marks (one part correct). Two batches must be added.

subQuestions.questionText:
Helen decided to change suppliers in September 2024 after receiving advice from her sister, the store manager.

• Provide TWO points that show her customers are unhappy with the quality of the headphones purchased from the new suppliers. Quote figures.
• What advice would you give to Helen about changing the supplier in the future? Provide ONE point.
subQuestions.memoText:
PART 1 — TWO points showing customer dissatisfaction (4 marks):

Any TWO relevant points with figures:
• 80 units were returned / R11 200 had to be refunded.
• Closing stock has increased (from 170 units) to 350 units / by 180 units / by 106%.
• 350 of the 620 (56%) units available for sale remain unsold.
• 310 new units sold (R68 200) compared to 680 old units sold (R149 600) — sales decreased by 370 units (R81 400).

PART 2 — Advice on changing supplier (2 marks):

Any ONE relevant point:
• Ensure that the quality of the headphones is not going to be compromised.
• Her decision must not be influenced by family or employees, but should be based on an informed decision/her own research.
• Do background checks on new suppliers before changing.
• Compare warranty of new suppliers with that from current supplier.
• Conduct market research to ensure new headphones meet market demand.
• Evaluate product performance through customer response before buying in bulk.

subQuestions.questionText:
TELEVISION SETS — The stock of TVs is valued using the specific identification method. The business sold two models (Quantum and Crystal) from 1 March 2024. A new model, Limpid, was introduced on 1 December 2024 to replace the Quantum.

Calculate the closing stock of the television sets on 28 February 2025.

INFORMATION:
A. Opening stock (1 March 2024): Quantum: 123 units at R4 800 = R590 400; Crystal: 72 units at R6 500 = R468 000.
B. Purchases: 1 July 2024 — Crystal: 186 units at R6 500 = R1 209 000; 1 Dec 2024 — Limpid: 115 units at R7 200 = R828 000.
C. Sales: Quantum: 105 units at R5 950 = R624 750; Crystal: 225 units at R9 750 = R2 193 750; Limpid: 94 units at R10 500 = R987 000.
D. Donation: Helen donated the unsold Quantum TVs to local high schools.
subQuestions.memoText:
Closing stock calculation by model:

Quantum: All unsold Quantum TVs (123 - 105 = 18 units) were donated. Therefore closing stock = R0.

Crystal: 
Available: 72 + 186 = 258 units
Sold: 225 units
Closing: 258 - 225 = 33 units
Value: 33 x R6 500 = R214 500
Alternative: (468 000 + 1 209 000) - (2 193 750 x 6 500/9 750) = 1 677 000 - 1 462 500 = R214 500

Limpid:
Available: 115 units
Sold: 94 units
Closing: 115 - 94 = 21 units
Value: 21 x R7 200 = R151 200
Alternative: 828 000 - (987 000 x 7 200/10 500) = 828 000 - 676 800 = R151 200

TOTAL CLOSING STOCK = 0 + R214 500 + R151 200 = R365 700

Mark allocation: 9 marks (one part correct).
Note: Award one method mark for 54 if shown as final answer. Superfluous entry; lose method on total.

subQuestions.questionText:
Helen was not satisfied that she was selling an average of 19 Crystal TVs per month. However, she is happy that the new Limpid TVs, despite its higher selling price per unit, is selling at a quicker rate than Crystal TVs.

• Calculate the cost of sales of the Limpid TVs.
• Calculate how long (in days) it will take Helen to sell the closing stock of the Limpid TVs.
• Helen feels that she has made a wise decision by replacing the Quantum TVs with the Limpid TVs. Give ONE possible reason (with figures) to substantiate her opinion.
subQuestions.memoText:
PART 1 — Cost of sales of Limpid TVs (3 marks):

Cost of Sales (Limpid) = Total available - Closing stock
= R828 000 - R151 200 (from 3.3)
= R676 800

Alternative calculations:
• 94 units x R7 200 = R676 800
• 987 000 x (7 200/10 500) = R676 800

PART 2 — Days to sell closing stock of Limpid (4 marks):

Limpid was introduced 1 December 2024 and stock period is 90 days (1 Dec - 28 Feb).

Days = (Closing stock / Cost of sales) x 90
= (R151 200 / R676 800) x 90
= 20.1 days (Accept 20 days)

Alternative: (21 / 94) x 90 = 20.1 days

PART 3 — ONE reason with figures (2 marks):

Any ONE reason with figures:
• Higher profit earned per unit (Quantum: R1 150 / Limpid: R3 300).
• Higher average monthly sales (Quantum units: 11.7 (or 8.8) / Limpid: 31).
• Unsold stock of Quantum (18 units) had to be donated.

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to information D. (Helen donated the unsold Quantum TVs to local high schools.)

Explain how this will have a positive effect on her business. Provide ONE point.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE relevant point (2 marks):
• Corporate social responsibility / increased support from the community / increased customer loyalty / increase in sales.
• Creates a positive image as latest technology is sold / will enhance brand perception.
• Increase reputation as a business that cares for the community / increased opportunity to gain positive publicity.
• Can result in tax benefits / result in lower taxable income.

subQuestions.questionText:
VACUUM CLEANERS

• Identify ONE problem with vacuum cleaners. Quote figures.
• What advice would you give? State ONE point.

INFORMATION (Vacuum Cleaners — 28 Feb 2025 vs 29 Feb 2024):
- Gross units sold: 532 / 565
- Cash sales units: 280 / 360
- Trade discount on cash sales: 5% / 5%
- Credit sales units: 230 / 190
- Payment policy: 90 days / 90 days
- Interest rate: 18% / 18%
- Returns (faulty units): 22 / 15
- Mark-up: 50% / 60%
subQuestions.memoText:
Identify ONE problem with figures + ONE advice (3 marks):

Possible PROBLEMS (with figures):
• Decrease of 80 units (22.2%) in cash sales / increase of 40 units (21.1%) in credit sales.

subQuestions.questionText:
Daisy MacDonald owns Canary Stores that sells school bags. The information relates to the budget period ending 31 July 2025.

Explain how the preparation of a Cash Budget serves as a management tool in assisting the business to manage its cash resources. State ONE point.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any ONE valid point (2 marks). Part-marks for partial/unclear answer:
• Can be used as a control measure to see if spending and receipts are going according to plan and to make necessary changes timeously.

subQuestions.questionText: Identify TWO items in the payment section of this Cash Budget which will not appear in the Projected Statement of Comprehensive Income.
subQuestions.memoText:
Any TWO items (2 marks):
• Loan repayment
• Deposit for vehicle

subQuestions.topic: Budgeting — Cash Budget vs Income Statement

subQuestions.questionText:
Complete the Creditors' Payment Schedule.

INFORMATION:
A. Sales: April R180 000; May R202 500; June ?; July R270 000. Mark-up 50% on cost. 20% of purchases cash, 80% credit. Stock replaced monthly.
B. Creditors' payment terms: 75% in month of purchase (5% discount); 15% one month after; 10% two months after.

Given that June total sales = ? (must be calculated). The schedule should show payments for June and July from credit purchases made in April, May, June and July.
subQuestions.memoText:
CREDITORS' PAYMENT SCHEDULE:

First, calculate credit purchases per month:
Cost of sales = Sales / 1.5
April: 180 000/1.5 = R120 000 total purchases x 80% = R96 000 credit purchases
May: 202 500/1.5 = R135 000 total purchases x 80% = R108 000 credit purchases
June: 225 000/1.5 = R150 000 x 80% = R120 000 credit purchases
July: 270 000/1.5 = R180 000 x 80% = R144 000 credit purchases

SCHEDULE:
Month | Credit Purchases | June | July
April | 96 000 | 9 600 (10%) |
May | 108 000 | 16 200 (15%) | 10 800 (10%)
June | 120 000 | 85 500 (75% x 95%) | 18 000 (15%)
July | 144 000 | | 102 600 (75% x 95%)

TOTAL: June = R111 300; July = R131 400

Note: 75% paid in same month with 5% discount: 75% x 95% = 71.25% of credit purchases
• June column 'June 75%': 120 000 x 75% x 95% = R85 500
• July column 'July 75%': 144 000 x 75% x 95% = R102 600

Mark allocation: 9 marks (one part correct).
Superfluous entry (April in July column); lose method on total.

subQuestions.questionText:
Calculate the missing figures (i) to (iv) in the Cash Budget.

(i) Cash sales for July 2025
(ii) Salaries and wages for June 2025 (given July figure: R35 280)
(iii) Repayment of loan on 1 July 2025 (Interest June R3 150; July R2 250; rate 15% p.a.)
(iv) Deposit for vehicle on 31 July 2025 (10% deposit; balance R6 875/month over 36 months)

INFORMATION:
C. Salaries: 5% increase from 1 July 2025. Two assistants in June; additional assistant from 1 July at same monthly salary as the other two after the increase.
D. Loan: Part repaid 1 July 2025. 15% p.a. interest paid monthly, not capitalised.
E. Vehicle: 10% deposit on 31 July; balance over 36 months at R6 875.
subQuestions.memoText:
(i) Cash sales for July 2025 (2 marks):
July sales = R270 000; Cash sales = 40%
Cash sales = R270 000 x 40% = R108 000
Alternative: 144 000 x (60/80) OR 270 000 - 162 000

(ii) Salaries and wages for June 2025 (4 marks):
July figure R35 280 represents 3 assistants at the new (post-5% increase) rate.
New salary per assistant = R35 280 / 3 = R11 760
Old salary per assistant = R11 760 x (100/105) = R11 200
June figure (2 assistants at old rate) = R11 200 x 2 = R22 400

Alternative: (11 760 - 560) x 2 = R22 400
Alternative: 35 280 x (200/315) = R22 400

(iii) Repayment of loan on 1 July 2025 (4 marks):
Decrease in monthly interest = R3 150 - R2 250 = R900
This represents 15%/12 = 1.25% per month of the principal repaid.
Loan repayment = R900 x (100/15) x 12 = R72 000

Alternative: 252 000 - 180 000 = R72 000

(iv) Deposit for vehicle on 31 July 2025 (4 marks):
Monthly instalment R6 875 represents 90% of vehicle cost over 36 months.
Vehicle cost = R6 875 x 36 / 90% × 100% 
Deposit = (R6 875 x 36) x (10/90) = R247 500 x (10/90) = R27 500

Alternative: 247 500 x (100/90) x (10/100) = R27 500
Alternative: R6 875 x 4 = R27 500

Mark allocation: 14 marks total (one part correct each).

subQuestions.questionText:
Refer to Information F.

The business rents 180 m² of the premises at a fixed rate per m². Rental agency planned increase from 1 August 2025. The owner reduced m² being rented from 1 July 2025.

Given: Rent expense June R59 940; July R47 952.

Calculate the reduction in the floor space (in m²) being rented during July 2025.
subQuestions.memoText:
Calculation of reduction in floor space (5 marks):

Reduction in rent = R59 940 - R47 952 = R11 988
Rate per m² = R59 940 / 180 = R333 per m²
Reduction in floor space = R11 988 / R333 = 36 m²

Alternative methods:
• 47 952 / 333 = 144 m²; reduction = 180 - 144 = 36 m²
• % reduction = (11 988/59 940) x 100 = 20%; reduction = 180 x 20% = 36 m²

Mark allocation: 5 marks (one part correct).
